newsitem.title: UK: Mideast tankers steady, UKC activity picks up.
newsitem.headline: Mideast tankers steady, UKC activity picks up.

text.p: Crude tanker fixing in the Middle East Gulf remained good and rates were steady.
In other loading sectors rates were unchanged and activity in line with a Monday apart from a healthier U.K/continent.
Most charterers in the Middle East Gulf appear to have received their October stem dates and, following the thinning of tonnage last week, some shipbrokers were cautiously hopeful of stronger rates.
But tonnage supply in the region was still seen to be good and several 1970s VLCCs are sitting spot, threatening to limit any push by owners of more modern vessels for highe rates.
Rates for VLCCs were broadly steady, around W55 to Japan, W50 to Singapore.

The U.K/continent showed a more bouyant tone with a number of aframaxes (80,000 tonners) getting fixed on inter UKC trips. Rates rose marginally to around W100 after weeks of hovering in the W90s. Brokers say there are plenty of vessels to take up any increase in fixing and do not expect a sharp rise in rates.
"There's a fair amount of tonnage to be got through before we see charterers scrambling for ships," said one broker.
The Caribbean up U.S. coast market saw rates slip slightly to W140, in part a response to the poor level of fixing.
But this sector is still far more attractive than other aframax markets.

Chartering interest has failed to ignite in the Mediterranean and requirements for both aframaxes and suezmaxes was noticeably absent. Brokers said 80,000 tonners going cross Med would have to settle for around W95.

West African activity was fair with rates steady. VLCCs had threatened to knock suezmaxes out of the market in recent weeks after a couple of VLCCs were fixed into Taiwan. VLCCs to the U.S were unchanged around W62.5 with 130,000 tonners at W85-87.5.
